key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while improving electronic uniformity, showing that smoother films are not necessarily electronically better.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother surfaces.
method: Form Ruddlesden–Popper caps using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium on 3D perovskites.
Compare statistical AFM topography with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite greater roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, retaining optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative device-efficiency or operational-lifetime results, so photovoltaic benefits require device-level validation.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
